alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued August 30 at 11:36AM MDT until September 1 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas,
Central Colorado River Basin, Central Gunnison and Uncompahgre
River Basin, Central Yampa River Basin, Debeque to Silt Corridor,
Flat Tops, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, Gore and Elk
Mountains/Central Mountain Valleys, Grand Valley, Grand and
Battlement Mesas, Northwest San Juan Mountains, Paradox
Valley/Lower Dolores River, Roan and Tavaputs Plateaus, Southwest
San Juan Mountains, Uncompahgre Plateau and Dallas Divide, Upper
Gunnison River Valley and West Elk and Sawatch Mountains and Utah,
including the following areas, Arches/Grand Flat,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains, Southeast
Utah and Tavaputs Plateau.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Recent burn scars will also be especially susceptible and these
include the Lee and Elk RX, Gold Mountain and Elk, Ferris, and
Babylon burn scars to name a few.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Monsoonal moisture will remain across the area through Monday
evening and will support thunderstorms and showers with heavy
rainfall across the watch area. Several rounds of heavier rain
are expected increasing the chance for flash flooding especially
in our more susceptible areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

afd.snippet: 000 FXUS65 KBOU 301948 AFDBOU Area Forecast Discussion National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO 148 PM MDT Sun Aug 30 2026 .KEY MESSAGES... - Scattered showers and storms capable of producing strong to severe wind gusts are expected to continue through the evening. - Better precipitation chances on Monday, with another round of afternoon/evening showers and storms, a few may become severe. - War

fwf.snippet: .DISCUSSION...Rest of today through Monday... Widespread showers and thunderstorms are expected to continue across the mountains today, with scattered showers and storms across the lower elevations. There are good chances (40-60%) of wetting rainfall across most of the high country north of I-70. Minimum humidity should remain above 20% across the plains and generally will remain near or above 40%

alerts.title: US 40 Milner Resurfacing-143246
alerts.description: Between Moonlight Way (1 mile west of the Steamboat Springs area) and County Road 29 (5 miles west of the Hayden area) from Mile Point 127.3 to Mile Point 100.4. Paving operations. Starting August 31, 2026 at 7:00PM MDT until September 1, 2026 at about 6:00AM MDT. Full schedule below: • August 31, 7:00PM - September 1, 6:00AM Comment: Work includes barrier placement for the slope stabilization and work on the bridge at MP 113 on the west end of the project limits. Nighttime hours will be 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. Vehicles will be reduced to a single-lane, alternating traffic intermittently in either direction, throughout the duration of the project Lane closures, guided by flaggers, will have up to 10-minute delays. The speed limit will be reduced to 40 mph through the work zone. The project is expected to last until the middle of November.

alerts.title: US 40 over Shelton Ditch-143210
alerts.description: Between County Road 51A and Shelton Lane (near Hayden) from Mile Point 108.5 to Mile Point 108.3. Road construction. Starting September 1, 2026 at 7:00AM MDT until September 1, 2026 at about 7:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • September 1, 7:00AM - September 1, 7:00PM Comment: Daytime work hours will be 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. in order to accommodate the commuter traffic on the US 40 corridor, Monday through Friday. Vehicles will be reduced to a single-lane, alternating traffic intermittently in either direction while the temporary detour is being built. The speed limit will be reduced to 30 mph through the work zone. The project is expected to last until early October. Several other projects are occurring this season on the US 40 corridor. For more information on these projects, please visit: www.cotrip.org
